steps.name: System tools resolve outside the workspace
steps.run: for c in sha256sum tar curl git grep date tr cut sort head mktemp rm touch sed; do p=$(command -v "$c") || exit 1; case "$p" in /*) ;; *) echo "$c is not a file: $p"; exit 1;; esac; case "$p" in "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"/*) echo "$c resolves inside the workspace: $p"; exit 1;; esac; done

steps.name: Stale gitleaks ignore entries (each commit must exist on a fetched branch and not on main; entries expire)
steps.run:
fail=0
[ "$(git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository)" = false ] || { echo "shallow clone: the history checks below would be blind"; fail=1; }
git rev-parse --verify -q refs/remotes/origin/main > /dev/null || { echo "origin/main is missing"; fail=1; }
[ -f .gitleaksignore ] || { echo ".gitleaksignore is missing"; fail=1; touch .gitleaksignore; }
# any line that is not blank, not a comment and not a 40-hex fingerprint entry escapes the checks below
if grep -nvE '^(#|$|[0-9a-f]{40}:[^:]+:(generic-api-key|curl-auth-user|private-key):[0-9]+$)' .gitleaksignore | cut -d: -f1 | grep .; then echo "malformed gitleaks ignore line(s) at the line numbers above (entry = <40-hex sha>:<path>:<generic-api-key|curl-auth-user|private-key>:<line>)"; fail=1; fi
# An entry is accepted only when its commit is on one of the three fixed named branches. A commit that is only on a
# wip/cloud-* lane branch is stale: gitleaks scans the history of HEAD, and a HEAD commit with a handover note fails the
# checks below anyway, so a lane-only entry has no legitimate use. A sha that is not in this clone is stale (the step goes on).
# Why the fixed names alone are not enough: anyone who can push one of those names (a repository ruleset should stop that)
# could point it at a commit of this pull request. So an entry for a commit that is part of this pull request's own history
# (an ancestor of HEAD) is accepted only when the identical line is already in .gitleaksignore on origin/main. An entry hides a
# finding on another branch, which is what the fixed names are for; a secret that would reach main is in the history of HEAD.
# git merge-base answers 0 (is an ancestor) or 1 (is not); any other answer is an error and fails the step with its message.
anc() {
  local rc=0
  git merge-base --is-ancestor "$1" "$2" || rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -le 1 ] || { echo "git merge-base failed (exit $rc) for $1 and $2"; fail=1; }
  return "$rc"
}
main_ignore=$(git show refs/remotes/origin/main:.gitleaksignore 2>/dev/null) || main_ignore=
while IFS= read -r entry; do
  sha=${entry%%:*}
  branches=$(git branch -r --contains "$sha" 2>/dev/null) || branches=
  grep -qE '^ *origin/(core/cloud-handover|handover-src/c1a-8460813|core/P2d-1)$' <<< "$branches" || { echo "stale ignore entry (not on a named handover branch): $sha"; fail=1; }
  git cat-file -e "$sha^{commit}" 2>/dev/null || continue
  if anc "$sha" refs/remotes/origin/main; then echo "ignore entry is in main history (needs an owner decision): $sha"; fail=1
  elif anc "$sha" HEAD && ! grep -qxF -- "$entry" <<< "$main_ignore"; then echo "ignore entry hides a commit in this pull request's own history: $sha"; fail=1; fi
done < <(grep -E '^[0-9a-f]{40}:' .gitleaksignore | sort -u)
[ "$(grep -cE '^# EXPIRES ' .gitleaksignore || true)" -le 1 ] || { echo "more than one EXPIRES line"; fail=1; }
exp=$(grep -oE '^# EXPIRES [0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$' .gitleaksignore | head -1 | cut -d' ' -f3 || true)
if [ -n "$exp" ] && [ "$(date -u -d "$exp" +%F 2>/dev/null)" != "$exp" ]; then echo "EXPIRES is not a real date: $exp"; fail=1; fi
if [ -z "$exp" ] && grep -qE '^[0-9a-f]{40}:' .gitleaksignore; then echo "entries exist but no '# EXPIRES YYYY-MM-DD' line"; fail=1; fi
if [ -n "$exp" ] && [ "$(date -u +%F)" \> "$exp" ]; then echo "gitleaks ignore entries expired on $exp"; fail=1; fi
if [ -n "$exp" ] && [ "$exp" \> "$(date -u -d '+90 days' +%F)" ]; then echo "EXPIRES is more than 90 days ahead: $exp"; fail=1; fi
# The temporary allowlist in .gitleaks.toml lives and dies with branch core/cloud-handover and the same EXPIRES date. Only
# these two rules depend on the file: the path checks below run whatever .gitleaks.toml says. This step does NOT make
# .gitleaks.toml (or .gitleaksignore, or inline gitleaks:allow comments) trustworthy: a pull request can still change them.
# That is the owner's review of those files (CODEOWNERS with required review, see the lead actions below). Full names
# refs/remotes/origin/... are used everywhere: a tag called origin/main would otherwise win over the branch.
# The test below also fires for an unrelated allowlist whose text has targetRules or handover/ in it: the message names the
# pattern that was found, it does not say who owns that allowlist.
[ -f .gitleaks.toml ] || { echo ".gitleaks.toml is missing"; fail=1; touch .gitleaks.toml; }
have_branch=1
git rev-parse --verify -q refs/remotes/origin/core/cloud-handover > /dev/null || have_branch=0
if grep -qE 'targetRules|handover/' .gitleaks.toml; then
  [ "$have_branch" = 1 ] || { echo "an allowlist mentioning targetRules or handover/ is in .gitleaks.toml and branch core/cloud-handover is missing: delete the allowlist or restore the branch"; fail=1; }
  [ -n "$exp" ] || { echo "temporary allowlist in .gitleaks.toml needs the EXPIRES date in .gitleaksignore"; fail=1; }
fi
# Handover notes must live only on core/cloud-handover and its wip/cloud-* lane branches: none may exist in this checkout's tree
# nor in the history of HEAD, and none in any other fetched branch (git errors fail the step; -z avoids path quoting). If
# core/cloud-handover itself were a pull request head this step would fail, by design.
pat='^handover/(reviews|tickets|evidence)/'
gl_tmp=$(mktemp)
# show_where <paths file> <revision arguments>: the first five offending paths and the remote branches that hold them
show_where() {
  local f=$1 p c refs
  shift
  tr '\0' '\n' < "$f" | grep -E "$pat" | sort -u | head -5 | while IFS= read -r p; do
    c=$(git log -m --format=%H -1 "$@" -- ":(literal)$p" || true)
    refs=$(git branch -r --contains "$c" 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^ *//' | tr '\n' ' ' || true)
    refs=${refs% }; echo "  $p (on: ${refs:-no remote branch})"
  done
}
git ls-tree -r -z --name-only HEAD > "$gl_tmp" || { echo "git ls-tree failed"; fail=1; }
if tr '\0' '\n' < "$gl_tmp" | grep -qE "$pat"; then echo "handover notes are in this checkout's tree (they may live only on core/cloud-handover and its wip/cloud-* lane branches):"; show_where "$gl_tmp" HEAD; fail=1; fi
# Hygiene only, not the control: branches named wip/cloud-<letters, digits, . _ -> are handover lane refs (same notes as
# core/cloud-handover, never merged into main) and are subtracted from this range, so their notes are not listed for every
# pull request; the two other fixed names are trusted for ignore entries only, not here. The refs are listed by name and
# filtered with a strict pattern (the git glob would also match an empty suffix and a name with a slash), then passed as plain
# arguments. Effect by design: a branch or tag pushed with a handover note under any other name makes this range check fail for
# every pull request until it is deleted (the message names the refs).
# Lead actions (repository settings, not done by this file; exception: needs the owner): a ruleset that restricts create,
# update and delete (no force push) of wip/cloud-*, core/cloud-handover, handover-src/c1a-8460813 and core/P2d-1; a limit on
# creating tags whose names start with origin/ or wip/; CODEOWNERS with required review on .github/**, .gitleaks.toml and
# .gitleaksignore. Without the ruleset a writer could point a lane name at any branch tip and hide it from this range (the
# check of HEAD's own history below still holds).
range=(HEAD --all --not)
if [ "$have_branch" = 1 ]; then range+=(refs/remotes/origin/core/cloud-handover); fi
while read -r lane; do range+=("$lane"); done < <(git for-each-ref --format='%(refname)' refs/remotes/origin | grep -E '^refs/remotes/origin/wip/cloud-[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$' || true)
git log -m --name-only -z --format= "${range[@]}" -- > "$gl_tmp" || { echo "git log failed"; fail=1; }
if tr '\0' '\n' < "$gl_tmp" | grep -qE "$pat"; then echo "handover notes exist in the history of HEAD or of a branch other than core/cloud-handover and the wip/cloud-* lane branches (they may live only there):"; show_where "$gl_tmp" "${range[@]}"; fail=1; fi
# THE CONTROL: the range above subtracts every commit reachable from the lane refs, so a pull request built on lane commits
# would hide them there: the history of HEAD itself is checked again with nothing subtracted
git log -m --name-only -z --format= HEAD -- > "$gl_tmp" || { echo "git log of HEAD failed"; fail=1; }
if tr '\0' '\n' < "$gl_tmp" | grep -qE "$pat"; then echo "handover notes exist in the history of HEAD itself (a lane branch does not excuse them; they may live only on core/cloud-handover and its wip/cloud-* lane branches):"; show_where "$gl_tmp" HEAD; fail=1; fi
rm -f "$gl_tmp"
exit "$fail"

steps.name: Secrets in the history of the checked-out head (gitleaks, checksum-verified binary)
steps.run:
curl -sSfL --retry 5 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 5 --connect-timeout 30 --proto "=https" --proto-redir "=https" --tlsv1.2 -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/gitleaks.tgz" \
  "https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/releases/download/v${GITLEAKS_VERSION}/gitleaks_${GITLEAKS_VERSION}_linux_x64.tar.gz"
echo "${GITLEAKS_SHA256}  $RUNNER_TEMP/gitleaks.tgz" | sha256sum -c -
tar -xzf "$RUNNER_TEMP/gitleaks.tgz" -C "$RUNNER_TEMP" gitleaks
# scope: only commits reachable from the checked-out head (--log-opts=HEAD). Without it gitleaks scans every fetched
# ref (--all), so another branch's content (handover notes, backup branches) fails every pull request.
"$RUNNER_TEMP/gitleaks" git --redact --no-banner --exit-code 1 --config .gitleaks.toml --log-opts=HEAD \
  --report-format json --report-path "$RUNNER_TEMP/gl.json" . || {
  # the secret itself is redacted; print only where it is, so a false positive can be fingerprinted
  python3 -c 'import json,sys; [print(f["RuleID"], f["File"], f["StartLine"], f["Commit"][:10], f["Fingerprint"]) for f in json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))]' "$RUNNER_TEMP/gl.json"
  exit 1
}

steps.name: Vulnerabilities, misconfigurations and secrets in the files (Trivy, checksum-verified binary)
steps.run:
curl -sSfL --retry 5 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 5 --connect-timeout 30 --proto "=https" --proto-redir "=https" --tlsv1.2 -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/trivy.tgz" \
  "https://github.com/aquasecurity/trivy/releases/download/v${TRIVY_VERSION}/trivy_${TRIVY_VERSION}_Linux-64bit.tar.gz"
echo "${TRIVY_SHA256}  $RUNNER_TEMP/trivy.tgz" | sha256sum -c -
tar -xzf "$RUNNER_TEMP/trivy.tgz" -C "$RUNNER_TEMP" trivy
"$RUNNER_TEMP/trivy" fs --skip-dirs .venv --scanners vuln,misconfig,secret --severity HIGH,CRITICAL --exit-code 1 --no-progress .
